fact: The National Identification Authority itself sets fees and runs first-time registration, card replacement, record updates and mobile registration at its district offices and Premium Centres.
The National Identification Authority's own PKI team is carrying out updates to the Ghana Card registration system, with services expected to resume on 10 May 2026.

NIA Executive Director Wisdom Yayra Koku told Metro TV on 17 September 2025 that NIA cleared a 640,000-card backlog by printing at its district offices, using 700,000 blank cards released by its private partner Identity Management Systems after negotiation.
Margins Group's CEO told MPs the company built and financed the registration system in 2019-2020 while the NIA operated it, and that the law gives the NIA the mandate over the database.

Ghana's National Identification Authority opened a Ghana Card registration centre in Spain, with applicants interviewed by officials in Accra and biometrics captured at the centre, per its Executive Secretary on X.
